name: Sensorineural Hearing Loss and Inner Ear Disorders

reference.source: Dhingra Diseases of ENT 8th Edition (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: Meniere tetrad: episodic vertigo, fluctuating loss, tinnitus, fullness
Sudden SNHL is emergency needing early steroids and MRI
Unilateral SNHL mandates neuroma exclusion imaging
Aminoglycoside ototoxicity hits high frequencies first
reference.pathophysiology: Endolymph volume expansion distends cochlear and vestibular compartments until membranes rupture mixing fluids and triggering attacks; hair cell death from ageing, noise, drugs or ischaemia removes transduction while nerve tumours compress conduction.
additionalDifferentials: Meniere versus BPPV by attack duration and hearing symptoms
Cochlear versus retrocochlear loss (reflex decay, MRI)
Ototoxic versus noise loss history patterns
additionalInvestigations: Pure tone and speech audiometry urgently for sudden loss
MRI internal auditory meatus with gadolinium for unilateral loss
Vestibular testing and high resolution CT for dehiscence
